title: Generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and Euclidean equality rigidity
main_claim: In a complete simply connected manifold with sec ≤ κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume, finite-perimeter set has perimeter at least the model profile I_{√−κ}(vol). In the Euclidean (κ=0) case, equality for a bounded set holds only for a region isometric to a round Euclidean ball. The proof rests on a sharp hypersurface Sobolev inequality (with an h²−b² potential), proved using conformal sphere maps and balancing, and then applied to confined isoperimetric minimizers.

issues.location: Sec. 4, Prop. confined-regularity; Sec. 7 Prop. equality-boundary; Sec. 9
issues.description: Key regularity and rearrangement inputs are imported from external results: Ghomi–Spruck Lemma 7.2(i),(ii) for obstacle C^{1,1} regularity near the confining sphere; Antonelli–Pasqualetto–Pozzetta Cor. 1.6 for local almost-minimizer regularity without a Ricci lower bound; Nobili–Violo Thm 1.1 for Pólya–Szegő. Their hypotheses are paraphrased rather than checked in the text. Also, Prop. 4.x establishes regularity only for the minimizer that Ghomi–Spruck supply, not for an arbitrary minimizer. That is enough, because Lemma profile-curvature only needs one regular minimizer at each differentiability volume.
issues.evidence: The paper states 'choose a minimizing region supplied by Ghomi–Spruck ... denote it by E'. The cited conclusions are standard for Λ-minimizers and obstacle problems, so no failure is identified.

coverage: I read every section (1–9) in full. Checked symbolically with sympy for b=0 and b=1: the radial identities u'=−A sn/(2D), u''=u'^2+u' cs/sn, and u' cs/sn=−½(b²+f²+u'²), plus the pullback identities 2z'/(1+z²)=f and 2z/(1+z²)=f·sn. Checked by hand: the Hessian inequality for u (radial equality, tangential part via Hessian comparison with u'≤0); the trace and integration by parts giving the completed square (cα=2, cα²=m−2); the inward-pointing argument on all three faces of the balancing cylinder (top-face bound −1/8); the second-variation algebra Q(ψw)≥(q−1)YB_w, which with c=q−2 gives ∫ψ²|dΦ|²≥Y and forces the square term to vanish, so the zero extension is constant (zero) — a contradiction that only needs a minimizer to exist; the Brezis–Lieb splitting step; the sign of the profile derivative (P'/V'>0); the contact bound h≤h0 from one-sided inward variations, with h≥1/R_B by obstacle comparison; area growth by deletion plus volume repair; the cutoff energy bound ≤2^m C Σ r^{m−2}; and W_b'=1/(m√(b²+(s_m/A)^{2/m})) with the ODE integration. Also checked: subadditivity of the model profile, the hole-filling step in 2D, the finite-volume cutoff via coarea, and the metric rescaling exponents. For the equality case: the almost-minimality constant (z^θ≥z for z<1); the Campanato difference-quotient argument for C^{1,1}; the flux lower moment ∫r²≥R²a; the second-order expansion of Sobolev at the constant function giving the gap m/R² (constants match since Y_m A^{2/q}=mA/R²); the barycenter coordinates giving the upper moment; the 2D Wirtinger argument giving L≥2πR; the 3D punctured flux (div Y≥2t², 2ht−2t²=h²/2−2(t−h/2)², J_ε→2π, h²A/2=2π) and the offset-sphere completing-the-square; phase recovery; and the volume/determinant argument forcing an isometry.
